narr: Light precipitation started to arrive on the evening of February 14th due to an approaching low pressure system, with more substantial rain spreading across the area overnight into the 15th as a warm front approached from the south. This promoted a brief instance of thunderstorms on the morning of February 15th, with damaging winds knocking down trees and power lines to parts of the state. While shower coverage diminished from southeast Ohio and northwest West Virginia during the afternoon, moderate to heavy rain continued to trail across northeast Kentucky, southern West Virginia, and southwest Virginia. This precipitation band lifted north with a front during the night, then the passing low pushed additional showers through with a cold front on the 16th. Rain turned to snow as cold air moved in behind the front, then light snow showers lingered into the 17th.||Three to five inches of rain fell across portions of southeast West Virginia. Two to three inches fell in southwest West Virginia. North of I-64, amounts ranged from one to two inches. ||Widespread flooding led to many road closures across West Virginia. However, the worst impacts occurred in southeastern West Virginia where several communities experienced considerable to catastrophic damage. A flash flood emergency was issued for the community of Welch in McDowell County, WV, where flooding invaded multiple homes and businesses, stranded vehicles, and made roads impassable. A vehicle entered the floodwaters and was subsequently swept into the Tug Fork River, with only two of the five occupants surviving.
ev: Street flooding was observed in the Buffalo area.

Flash flooding was observed along Huff Creek in Mallory, and Route 44 closed due to high water in Switzer. In Omar, there were multiple reports of flooded roads and homes surrounded by water. A landslide also blocked a lens of North Bridge Street in Man.
High water was observed on Garfield Road.
Flooding was observed on Paint Creek Road southwest of Handley, at Green Valley Drive and Willow Lane near Saint Albans, and at the US 60 estbound exit to West Dupont Avenue in Belle.
High water was observed on Walkers Branch Road at Browning Dixon.
Flooding and debris occurred on Greenhills Road near the Greenhills Golf Course.
Centerville Road and Whites Creek Road flooded.

Flash flooding impacted Ritter Drive and C and O Dam Road near Whitney Court in Daniels, Airport Road and Violet Lane in Beaver, Coal River Road near McGraw Court near Stover, Vanwood Street in Mead, Tommy Creek Road in Rhodell, Stotesbury Road near Sophia, and Wickham Road in Wickham. A mudslide also occurred on Friendly View Road near Dry Creek.
Water was observed covering Coal River Road near Alum Creek.
Street flooding was observed within Parchment Valley.
Multiple sections of US 152, in the Moses Fork area, were covered by water. Jennies Creek exceeded its banks and flooded the road.

Major flash flooding occurred in and around Welch. Homes and businesses were surrounded by water, roads and underpasses became impassable, and cars were stranded. People became trapped in their vehicles on Riverside Drive before the Havaco bridge. In Kimball, water entered multiple homes, businesses, and cars. A vehicle with five occupants drove into floodwaters and was swept into the Tug Fork River. Two people were able to make it to safety while the other three occupants perished.

Water covered Mate Hatfield Lane and Bulldog Boulevard near Delbarton, the Left Fork of Bens Creek Road off King Coal Highway, and Parsley Bottom near Lenore. Multiple areas of Rutherford Hollow flooded. Water rose to the headlights of a lifted truck near Mullins Tire. Residences on State Route 65 in Red Jacket also flooded.
